body.p: After the aforesaid amendments, claims 1 and 3-20 are currently pending in the present application, of which claims 16-20 are withdrawn from consideration as being directed to non- elected subject matters.

Independent claim 1 is currently amended to include the limitations of "the interface unit configured for the examinee returning a response message according to the inquiry and acquiring a physiological characteristic related to one or both eyes of the examinee to generate at least one of a physiological characteristic signal," "a diagnosis module connected to the intelligent calculation module and the user module, and configured to receive the analysis report for assisting the examiner for diagnosis and send a diagnosis notification to the user module" and "the diagnosis notification is returned to the intelligent calculation module, and the intelligent calculation module is trained by the diagnosis notification based on the examination items," by reference to original claims 2, 5, and 15 of the present application.

Accordingly, claim 2 is canceled, and claim 15 is amended to depend upon the amended independent claim 1 and recite "the intelligent calculation module is trained by the diagnosis notification based on at least one of the response message and the physiological characteristic signal."
In addition, independent claim 1 is further amended to rephrase some of the recitations
for clarification.
The aforementioned amendments can be fully supported by the original disclosure of the present application. No new matter is being introduced.

Claims 1-9 and 11-15 are rejected under 35 U.S. C. 103 as being unpatentable over Tang et al. (US2018/0046773) in view of Rao et al. (US2019/0110754), and claim 10 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Tang in view of Coleman et al. (US2019/0113973).
The rejections are respectfully traversed for the following reasons.
As recited in the amended independent claim 1 of the present application, the claimed invention is directed to a neurological disorders decision support system for assisting an

examiner to diagnose an examinee. Specifically, the neurological disorders decision support system of the claimed invention comprises a user module, a screening module, an intelligent calculation module, and a diagnosis module, inter alia:

the user module comprising an indication unit and an interface unit, the indication unit configured to issue an inquiry to the examinee according to a first indication signal, and the interface unit configured for the examinee returning a response message according to the inquiry and acquiring a physiological characteristic related to one or both eves of the examinee to generate at least one of a physiological characteristic signal;

the screening module configured to generate the first indication signal and output the first indication signal to the indication unit, and the screening module further configured to execute a neurological examination application program and generate a second indication signal according to the response message to the indication unit, wherein the neurological examination application program provides a plurality of examination items and selects one or more examination items from the plurality of examination items based on the response message;

the intelligent calculation module configured to execute an algorithm to calculate at least one of the response message, the physiological characteristic signal and the examination items to generate an analysis report to the examiner; and

the diagnosis module configured to receive the analysis report for assisting the examiner for diagnosis and send a diagnosis notification to the user module, wherein the diagnosis notification is returned to the intelligent calculation module, and the intelligent calculation module is trained by the diagnosis notification based on the examination items.
(Emphasis added.)

It is thus noted that the interface unit of the claimed user module in the present application is configured for the examinee to return a response message according to the inquiry and acquire a physiological characteristic related to one or both eyes of the examinee to

generate at least one of a physiological characteristic signal. However, Tang merely discloses in Table 5 with respect to the eye redness for fever as an initial symptom. Obviously, nowhere in Tang provides any teachings or suggestions that relate the eye of an examinee to a neurological disorder as claimed in the present application.

In addition, as acknowledged by the examiner on page 5 of this Office Action, Tang simply teaches analyzing the user's symptoms but fails to explicitly disclose the limitations that "the neurological examination application program provides a plurality of examination items" and "the neurological examination application program selects one or more examination items from the examination items based on the response message," as recited in previously presented independent claim 1 of the present application. Therefore, Tang can never teach or

suggest the limitation of "the diagnosis module configured to receive the analysis report for assisting the examiner for diagnosis and send a diagnosis notification to the user module, wherein the diagnosis notification is returned to the intelligent calculation module, and the intelligent calculation module is trained by the diagnosis notification based on the examination items," as recited in the amended independent claim 1 of the present application.

As to Rao, it is directed to a system and methods for diagnosing and monitoring neurological disorders in a patient using an artificial intelligence-based system. Particularly, Rao provides a deep brain stimulation (DBS) device that is implanted in the patient's brain or nervous system, and the neurostimulation device disclosed in Rao delivers electrical current to specific regions of the brain or other parts of the nervous system for a therapeutic effect (referring to paragraph [0029] of the specification in Rao). Nevertheless, Rao is totally silent on the claimed diagnosis module of the present application that is configured to send a diagnosis notification to the user module, wherein the diagnosis notification is returned to the intelligent calculation module, and the intelligent calculation module is trained by the diagnosis notification based on the examination items. Therefore, Rao fails to cure the aforementioned deficiency of Tang, and thus the proposed combination of Tang and Rao still cannot render obvious the claimed invention recited in the amended independent claim 1 of the present application.

Regarding Coleman, it is only cited to be in combination with Tang for the §103 rejection of dependent claim 10. Specifically, Coleman is directed to a computer network implemented system for improving the operation of one or more biofeedback computer systems. However, similar to Tang, Coleman completely fails to provide any teachings or suggestions that relate the eye of an examinee to a neurological disorder as claimed in the present application. Moreover, Coleman also does not disclose the diagnosis module of the claimed invention that is configured to receive an analysis report for assisting the examiner for diagnosis and send a diagnosis notification to the user module, wherein the diagnosis notification is returned to the intelligent calculation module, and the intelligent calculation module is trained by the diagnosis notification based on the examination items. Therefore, Coleman still cannot remedy the aforementioned deficiency of Tang to render obvious the claimed invention of the present application.

Given the foregoing, Applicant respectfully submits that Tang, alone or in combination with Rao or Coleman, cannot render obvious the claimed invention recited in the amended independent claim 1 of the present application. Hence, the amended independent claim 1 and the dependent claims thereof are patentably distinct over the cited references. Accordingly, reconsideration and withdrawal of the §103 rejections are respectfully requested.

For further reference, the corresponding counterparts of the present application have been granted and issued in Japan as JP7362138B2 on October 17, 2023 and in Taiwan as TWI823015B on November 21, 2023.

Applicant expresses his gratitude to Examiner for the courtesies extended to the Applicant's undersigned representative throughout prosecution of this application. In view of the foregoing, Applicant respectfully submits that each of the pending rejections has been overcome, leaving the present application in condition for allowance. A consideration to that effect is respectfully requested.
